nodes.characterization_summary: RZW, RZ, and RW catalysts display typical rutile RuO₂ structure with no significant deviation from standard peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of all samples displayed a typical rutile structure with no significant deviation from the standard peaks of RuO₂ (PDF 01-070-2662)...

nodes.characterization_summary: RZW, RZ, and RW catalysts show stacked nanoparticle morphologies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images illustrated the stacked nanoparticle morphologies of the RZW, RZ and RW catalysts.

nodes.characterization_summary: RZW catalyst shows lattice fringes corresponding to (110) and (101) planes of rutile RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) further demonstrated the great crystallinity of the RZW, showcasing lattice fringes that correspond to the (110) and (101) planes of rutile RuO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: RZW catalyst displays diffraction rings indexed to (110), (101), and (211) planes of rutile RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This observation aligned with the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the RZW catalysts, which displayed distinct diffraction rings that can be indexed to the (110), (101), and (211) planes of the rutile RuO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms successful incorporation and uniform distribution of Zn and W within RuO₂ matrix of RZW catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping confirmed the successful incorporation and uniform distribution of Zn and W within the RuO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl values: RZW 34.3 mF cm⁻² (ECSA 192.1 cm²), RZ higher than RW and C-RuO₂ after OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 2e, the C_dl of the RZW catalysts was determined to be 34.3 mF cm⁻², resulting in a calculated ECSA of 192.1 cm², which surpassed that of the reference catalysts of RZ (115.4 cm²), RW (123.4 cm²), and C-RuO₂ (24.6 cm²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS shows Ru-O peak at 1.56 Å and Ru-Ru/Zn/W at 3.21 Å for RZW; Ru-O coordination number and bond length nearly unchanged in AR-RZW.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Figure 3a, two prominent peaks at 1.56 and 3.21 Å resemble those observed in the C-RuO₂ catalysts, indicating the presence of Ru-O and Ru-Ru/Zn/W coordination shells...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge WT-EXAFS confirms similar Ru-O and Ru-Ru/Zn/W scattering signals for RZW, RZ, RW, C-RuO₂, and AR-RZW.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the WT-EXAFS spectra at the Ru K-edge of the RZW catalysts displayed similar scattering signals for Ru-O and Ru-Ru/Zn/W as observed in the RZ, RW, and C-RuO₂ catalysts.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated Ru oxidation states for the RZW, RZ, and RW catalysts were +3.87, +3.83, and +3.59, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: ~32 wt% total Zn dissolved from RZW after OER stability test, ~95% in first hour, dissolution nearly ceases after 24 hours.
nodes.evidence_snippet: we employed inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) to monitor the time-dependent dissolution of metal ions during the OER stability test... Approximately 95% of the total dissolved Zn species underwent rapid dissolution during the first hour... After 24 hours of OER reaction, the dissolution of the metal in the RZW catalysts nearly ceased.
